A 25-year-old woman visits her primary care physician due to bilateral nipple discharge. She reports
noticing a milky discharge from her nipples over the past month. Additionally, she has been feeling
fatigued, has experienced decreased libido, and mentions morning headaches that typically resolve by
midday. She has also gained 5 pounds in the last month. Her medical history includes obesity,
schizophrenia, and constipation. On examination, her temperature is 98.3°F (37.5°C), blood pressure
is 130/93 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Physical examination reveals an obese woman with a fatigued appearance. Dermatologic findings
include fine, thin body hair. Cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable, and neurological
assessment shows intact cranial nerves 2-12. Reflexes are 1+ and sluggish. What is the most likely
diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Idiopathic hyperprolactinemia (B) Hypothyroidism-induced
galactorrhea (C) Protein-secreting CNS mass (D) Medication-induced hyperprolactinemia (E) Normal
pregnancy (F) Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) with hormonal imbalance (G) Hyperestrogenemia
from liver dysfunction (H) Dopamine blockade in the tuberoinfundibular pathway (I) Chronic kidney
disease causing secondary hyperprolactinemia (J) Pituitary adenoma causing hyperprolactinemia
 A. Protein-secreting CNS mass
B. Idiopathic hyperprolactinemia
C. Chronic kidney disease causing secondary hyperprolactinemia
D. Hyperestrogenemia from liver dysfunction
E. Medication-induced hyperprolactinemia
F. Hypothyroidism-induced galactorrhea
G. Pituitary adenoma causing hyperprolactinemia
H. Dopamine blockade in the tuberoinfundibular pathway
I. Normal pregnancy
J. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) with hormonal imbalance
